newsitem.title: USA: Klein likely Clinton choice for antitrust post.
newsitem.headline: Klein likely Clinton choice for antitrust post.

text.p: President Clinton has all but settled on Joel Klein to replace Anne Bingaman as antitrust chief in the Justice Department, a government source said.
Klein, a former deputy White House counsel who is serving as temporary head of the antitrust office, was the top choice among three finalists, sources said. A White House spokesman declined comment.

Other top choices were David Turetsky, a deputy assistant attorney general in the antitrust division who specialises in telecommuncations, and Janet McDavid, a lawyer at the Washington firm of Hogan and Hartson.

Klein, 50, who has been serving as acting antitrust chief since Bingaman left last year, has said in public statements that he sees telecommunications and international trust as important areas. His post is only one of the vacancies to be filled in rounding out the president's antitrust team.

The Justice Department has overlapping jurisdiction with the Federal Trade Commission on civil antitrust. Justice handles criminal antitrust, while the FTC has a special mandate for consumer protection.

Last month Clinton nominated Sheila Anthony, sister of late deputy White House counsel Vincent Foster, for the FTC job. She is known both for her expertise in intellectual property and her tenure as a top Justice Department official. The Senate Commerce Committee has yet to set a date yet for her confirmation hearings.
FTC Commissioner Christine Varney praised the choice of Anthony, saying she would bring an "intellectual property expertise that hasn't previously been here."

Terry Adamson, a lawyer at Kaye, Scholer who was at Justice in the 1970s, said he and Anthony set a precedent by stopping a "video clipping" service from taping and selling portions of television news broadcasts without permission.
"Her deep experience in the intellectual property and telecommunications fields is a tremendous asset," he said.

Anthony, 56, whose husband Beryl once served as a congressman from Arkansas, started out as a classroom teacher in the Arkansas Public School system. She would replace Janet Steiger, an appointee of President George Bush.
